notes.note: Moved TODO -> IN_PROGRESS on the 21 Aug 2026 working session. Both halves of this goal - set endpoint, configure webhook - are built and were exercised against the live Paperless instance. The endpoint is a subgraph shipped inside the integration package at /graphql/paperless-webhook, authenticated with a shared secret held per sync document rather than a single global token. The webhook side needs no manual Paperless admin work: the processor POSTs to /api/workflows/ to create a workflow with triggers Document Added and Document Updated and action type 4 (Webhook), and the call is idempotent on the workflow name, so re-running it does not accumulate duplicates. What remains is purely deployment-shaped: the workflow that was tested pointed at a localhost URL and was deleted afterwards, so it has to be recreated against the public URL of the deployed Switchboard. That depends on goal 2.c (c4fb39f7) being installed there first.

notes.note: Prototype built 21 Aug 2026, awaiting liberuum visual review - NOT accepted yet. Approach agreed beforehand: react-pdf (pdfjs-dist 5.4.296) + hybrid pane. Three new components in demos/billing: components/pdfPane.tsx (canvas render, one page at a time, zoom-only via +/-/wheel), components/splitPane.tsx (draggable divider, 30-70pct clamp, localStorage-persisted, keyboard accessible), components/paymentDetailsCard.tsx (surfaces bank/intermediary/wallet routing, which the PDF prints but the editor previously only showed inside the party modal). Key decision: NOT an iframe - the browser's built-in PDF viewer owns an iframe and its toolbar cannot be reliably suppressed (#toolbar=0 is a non-standard Chromium hint Firefox ignores), so canvas rendering is what makes zoom-only possible. PDFReviewModal left untouched because ingestPDF.tsx and timeTrackingReportButton.tsx also use it; only the View-Uploaded-Invoice path switched to the split view, and it still falls back to that modal below 1000px. Body JSX extracted to an invoiceBody value and reused in both layouts, so the pane is fully editable with one source of truth - the existing section grids are already auto-fit and collapse to one column unaided. Gates: tsc clean, 172/172 tests, zero lint findings on the new files, editor.tsx lint unchanged at 5 pre-existing warnings, ph-cli build emits the worker locally at dist/browser/assets/pdf.worker.min-*.mjs (no CDN). Known gaps: line-items table h-scrolls in the narrow pane rather than becoming cards (LineItemCard + LineItemMobileModal exist as dead code and are the intended upgrade); plain-wheel zoom preempts scroll-to-pan when zoomed in; pane height uses a 60vh floor rather than computed header offsets.

notes.note: Correction to the previous note after liberuum review, 21 Aug 2026: the PDF pane no longer shows one page at a time and no longer zooms on the scroll wheel. Both were wrong for the actual use case - in a multi-page invoice the wheel gesture is wanted for reaching the next page, and wheel-zoom stole it. pdfPane.tsx now renders every page in one continuous vertical scroll (per-page 'n / N' badge in the corner when multi-page), the wheel is left entirely to native scrolling, and zoom is explicit via the -/+ buttons with the percentage button resetting to fit-width. This also retires the 'plain-wheel zoom preempts scroll-to-pan' gap listed in the previous note. Note one consequence: react-pdf does not virtualise, so every page is canvas-rendered up front - fine for invoices (1-3 pages), worth revisiting if long attachments ever land here. Gates re-run after the change: tsc clean, 172/172 tests, zero lint findings on pdfPane.tsx, ph-cli build still emits the worker locally.

notes.note: Found 21 Aug 2026 while testing the compare view with a 10-page, 195-line-item sample invoice. Root cause proven, not inferred: document-models/invoice/v1/src/reducers/items.ts:133 validatePrices uses EPSILON=0.00001, which is ~1e-5 on values that real invoices state to 2 decimals. Worked example: 19.99 at 21% tax -> inclusive 24.19 -> 24.19/1.21 = 19.9917, which is 8.3e-4 away from 19.99, i.e. 83x the tolerance, so the item is rejected. Items only survive when the inclusive price divides back cleanly. This is exactly what liberuum observed: the extraction modal listed 10 line items, only 2 landed in state, and BOTH survivors were the only ones with taxPercent=0 (where inclusive==exclusive so all four checks hold trivially). Second half of the defect: editors/invoice-editor/ingestPDF.tsx:95 dispatches addLineItem in a forEach and never inspects the result, so the reducer throw is recorded on the operation as .error, state is left unchanged, and the UI reports success. Eight items vanished with no error surfaced anywhere. Suggested fix: widen EPSILON to a half-cent (0.005) or compare against rounded values, AND surface per-item failures from the ingest loop. Deliberately NOT attempted here: this is a document-model reducer, so per the repo CLAUDE.md it needs the two-step MCP process plus reducer coverage at or above 95pct, and it was liberuum's call to make. Note this matters in production, not just for synthetic fixtures - real invoices carry rounded taxed prices.
notes.author: knowledge-agent

goals.outcome: Fixed 21 Aug 2026 in commit e6541f9 (branch feat/invoice-pdf-compare-view). validatePrices now compares money in cents with tolerance scaling by quantity, because a unit price rounded by up to a cent becomes a line total off by up to a cent per unit. applyInvariants runs on add as well as edit and is now unconditional - any change-detection threshold lets drift smaller than itself persist into state, which is how a 9e-6 per-unit discrepancy survived and resurfaced as a multi-unit gap; re-deriving every time keeps stored values exactly consistent with unitPriceTaxExcl and taxPercent, which is what makes liberal validation safe. The fourth check was deleted as provably dead: comparing the two totals differs by qty*|excl-incl/(1+rate)| against a CENT*qty tolerance, so it fired on exactly the same condition as the unit-price check. Second half also fixed: applyExtractedInvoice now returns a report and console.warns anything skipped, so silent loss is visible, and its line-item fields are narrowed off any (which removed 33 pre-existing lint findings, 152 -> 119). Gates: tsc clean, 175/175 tests (the amplification test rewritten to assert normalisation instead of rejection, plus 3 regression tests including the 19.99-at-21pct case), reducer coverage 100pct on statements/branches/functions/lines - reached by deleting the unreachable branch, not by testing around it. NOTE: no MCP/model-JSON step was needed - invoice.json carries an empty reducer body for ADD_LINE_ITEM, so src/reducers/items.ts is the sole source of truth for this logic.
goals.description: validatePrices EPSILON=0.00001 silently drops line items with realistically-rounded taxed prices, and ingestPDF swallows the reducer errors (10 extracted -> 2 stored)
